articles.title: Hair-Pulling Brawl Between Two BLOs Caught on Camera During Voter List Meeting in Ballia
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A physical altercation between two female Booth Level Officers (BLOs) was caught on camera on Monday, February 16, 2026, during a Special Intensive Revision (SIR) meeting in Ballia, Uttar Pradesh.

body.html:
A physical altercation between two female Booth Level Officers (BLOs) was caught on camera on Monday, February 16, 2026, during a Special Intensive Revision (SIR) meeting in Ballia, Uttar Pradesh.

The incident took place at Composite School Bhrigu Ashram, where BLOs had gathered to sign notices and coordinate voter list revision work.

Dispute Over Work Allocation

The two BLOs involved have been identified as Suman Devi and Neelam Singh. According to Suman Devi, an argument broke out over the distribution of work notices. She alleged that she had been assigned 240 notices, while Neelam Singh had received over 400, leading to tension between them.

Suman further claimed that Neelam Singh made caste-based remarks, attacked her with a slipper, pulled her hair and pushed her against a wall. She said she managed to escape and later went to a hospital, where she was given preliminary medical attention. She has filed a formal police complaint.

Scuffle Captured on Video

A video of the incident, which has since gone viral, shows the two women pulling each other’s hair and engaging in a physical fight. More than a dozen men and women can be seen present at the scene, with some staff members attempting to separate them.

Police Action

Both parties have lodged complaints at the Kotwali Police Station Ballia.

Station House Officer Kshitij Tripathi confirmed that complaints have been received from both sides and that necessary legal action is being initiated. Police said the matter is under investigation.

articles.title: CCTV Exposes ‘Garbage Plot’ in Moradabad: Rival Shopkeeper Accused of Framing Juice Seller Under SB
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: In a shocking case from Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh, a juice and cold drink seller has alleged that a neighbouring shopkeeper conspired to frame him by getting garbage scattered outside his shop in an attempt to damage his business.

body.html:
In a shocking case from Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh, a juice and cold drink seller has alleged that a neighbouring shopkeeper conspired to frame him by getting garbage scattered outside his shop in an attempt to damage his business.

Talha, who runs a juice, cold drink and coffee shop in Budh Bazaar area of Moradabad, is known for attracting a steady crowd of customers. According to local sources, his growing popularity allegedly led to jealousy from a neighbouring shopkeeper.

As per the allegations, the neighbouring shopkeeper bribed sanitation workers and had them scatter garbage from a dustbin in front of Talha’s shop. Subsequently, a complaint was reportedly lodged with the municipal corporation under the Swachh Bharat Mission, accusing Talha of spreading filth.

Acting on the complaint, municipal corporation officials issued a notice and allegedly pressured Talha to vacate his shop. Refusing to comply, Talha approached the police.

When police examined the CCTV footage from the area, the alleged conspiracy came to light. The footage reportedly showed sanitation workers deliberately scattering garbage from the dustbin onto the road in front of Talha’s shop.

The incident has triggered outrage in Budh Bazaar, with questions being raised over the role of certain municipal officials.

Moradabad Police confirmed that the matter was examined after CCTV evidence surfaced. Moradabad Municipal Corporation has also come under scrutiny following the allegations.

According to local sources, the SP City, Moradabad, assured Talha that he would not be harassed without reason and that appropriate action would be taken based on evidence.

Further investigation is underway.

articles.title: Minor SUV Driver Gets Bail After 23-Year-Old Dies in Dwarka Crash; Grieving Mother Seeks Justice
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A 23-year-old man was killed in a road accident in Dwarka, Delhi, earlier this month after an SUV allegedly driven by a 17-year-old boy collided with his motorcycle and then rammed into a parked car. The deceased has been identified as Sahil Dhaneshra.

body.html:
A 23-year-old man was killed in a road accident in Dwarka, Delhi, earlier this month after an SUV allegedly driven by a 17-year-old boy collided with his motorcycle and then rammed into a parked car.

The deceased has been identified as Sahil Dhaneshra. His mother, in a social media video, alleged that her son was killed due to reckless driving and claimed that the minor was performing stunts for social media fame. Police, however, have stated that the matter remains under investigation.

“I raised my child for 23 years as a single mother. On February 3, my innocent child was blown away by a car. I am a helpless mother,” she said, appealing to media organisations and residents of Dwarka to support her in seeking justice. She also urged parents to be vigilant about road safety.

Accident Details

According to police, the fatal accident was reported at 11.57 am on February 3 near Lal Bahadur Shastri College under the jurisdiction of Dwarka South Police Station.

A police team reached the spot and found three vehicles — an SUV (Scorpio), a Dzire taxi and a motorcycle — in an accidental condition.

Sahil Dhaneshra, who was riding the motorcycle, was found dead at the scene. Ajit Singh, the driver of the parked Dzire taxi, sustained injuries and was shifted to Indira Gandhi International Hospital (IGI Hospital). His statement has been recorded and the final medical opinion on his medico-legal case (MLC) is awaited.

Minor Driver Apprehended

During investigation, the SUV driver was identified as 17-year-old Akshatra Singh. Police said he was driving without a valid licence at the time of the accident. Being a minor, he was produced before the Juvenile Justice Board and sent to an observation home.

On February 10, the JJB granted him interim bail, citing his ongoing Class 10 board examinations.

Legal Action and Probe

An FIR was registered under Sections 281 (rash driving), 106(1) (causing death by negligence) and 125(a) (act endangering life or personal safety of others) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).

All three vehicles involved in the accident have been seized and mechanically inspected. CCTV footage from the surrounding area has also been collected.

Preliminary findings suggest that the SUV first collided with the motorcycle coming from the opposite direction before hitting the parked Dzire car on the roadside.

Speaking to reports, DCP (Dwarka) Ankit Singh said further investigation into the circumstances leading to the accident is underway.

articles.title: Mosque Vandalised, Copies of Holy Quran Desecrated in Telangana Village; Beer Bottles Found Inside
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Worshippers at the Jama Masjid in Jalalpur village of Bommalaramaram Mandal, Yadadri Bhuvanagiri district, were shocked on Monday morning, February 16, 2026, after discovering that the mosque had been vandalised during the night.

body.html:
Worshippers at the Jama Masjid in Jalalpur village of Bommalaramaram Mandal, Yadadri Bhuvanagiri district, were shocked on Monday morning, February 16, 2026, after discovering that the mosque had been vandalised during the night.

According to local residents, unidentified miscreants allegedly broke into the mosque around midnight. The accused reportedly damaged walls, window panes, washroom doors and the microphone system inside the premises.

Multiple copies of the Holy Quran were found scattered and desecrated across the mosque compound. Empty beer and whisky bottles were also recovered from inside the place of worship, causing anger and distress among the local community.

Condemning the incident, Majlis Bachao Tehreek (MBT) spokesperson Amjed Ullah Khan demanded that the police register a criminal case and conduct a thorough investigation at the earliest.

An officer from Bommalaramaram Police said that a communal angle was being downplayed at this stage, stating that beer bottles were thrown inside the premises and that the mosque has since been cleaned.

Police have registered a First Information Report (FIR) against unknown persons under Sections 331(4) (house trespass or house-breaking), 329(4) (criminal trespass), 298 (injuring or defiling a place of worship), 324(4) (mischief) and 196 (promoting enmity between different groups on religious grounds) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).

Three special teams have been formed to trace and apprehend the miscreants. Investigation is underway.

articles.title: Uproar at Khereshwar Mahadev Temple: Undergarment Stall Sparks Major Clash
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A commotion broke out at the Khereshwar Mahadev Temple complex in Aligarh, Uttar Pradesh, after objections were raised over a stall allegedly selling women’s undergarments inside the premises.

body.html:
A commotion broke out at the Khereshwar Mahadev Temple complex in Aligarh, Uttar Pradesh, after objections were raised over a stall allegedly selling women’s undergarments inside the premises.

According to reports, a man identified as Armaan had set up the stall within the temple complex, located under the Lodha police station area. On Saturday night, Sachin Raghav, associated with the Karni Sena, along with four to five supporters, entered the temple premises and began protesting.

It is alleged that Raghav went to the temple’s lost and found centre, took the microphone from the announcer, and used it to voice objections. During the protest, an altercation reportedly broke out between members of the temple committee and Karni Sena workers.

Upon receiving information about the disturbance, local police reached the spot and detained three youths for allegedly creating a ruckus. The situation was brought under control after the stall was closed. The detained Karni Sena members were later sent to jail under sections related to disturbing the peace.

Speaking from custody, Sachin Raghav claimed that they were protesting against the stall operating inside the temple complex and alleged that they were being treated as criminals despite committing no offence.

Lodha police station in-charge Hemant Mavi stated that action was taken against the three individuals for disturbing public order. Further legal proceedings are underway.

articles.title: “20 Quarters Do, Nahin Toh Jail!” – UP Inspector’s Alleged Audio Sparks Outrage
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Serious allegations have surfaced against Sub-Inspector Jagdish Verma, posted at the Kaimganj police station in Farrukhabad district, Uttar Pradesh. An audio clip, which has gone viral on social media, allegedly captures the officer demanding 20 quarters of liquor from a canteen operator.

body.html:
Serious allegations have surfaced against Sub-Inspector Jagdish Verma, posted at the Kaimganj police station in Farrukhabad district, Uttar Pradesh. An audio clip, which has gone viral on social media, allegedly captures the officer demanding 20 quarters of liquor from a canteen operator.

According to the allegations, the officer first tried to persuade the canteen operator politely. When the request was reportedly refused, he allegedly threatened to send him to jail. The viral audio has triggered sharp reactions and raised questions about the functioning of the local police.

There are also claims of possible collusion with liquor shops and misuse of authority, though these allegations are yet to be officially verified. The incident is said to be related to the Kaimganj police station area.

Following the circulation of the audio, Fatehgarh Police stated that instructions have been issued to investigate the matter. Authorities said further legal action will be taken based on the findings of the enquiry.

Demands for a thorough and transparent investigation have intensified as the clip continues to circulate online.

articles.title: Major tragedy in Bhiwadi, Rajasthan 🚨
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A devastating explosion ripped through an illegal firecracker manufacturing unit on February 16 in the Khushkhera-Karoli Industrial Area of Alwar district, killing at least 7–8 workers.

body.html:
A devastating explosion ripped through an illegal firecracker manufacturing unit on February 16 in the Khushkhera-Karoli Industrial Area of Alwar district, killing at least 7–8 workers.

Officials said the factory was officially registered as a readymade garment unit but was allegedly being used to manufacture firecrackers illegally. Preliminary findings indicate the presence of gunpowder and packing materials at the site. There are also suspicions that workers may have been locked inside while working.

Due to the intensity of the blaze, several victims were burned beyond recognition, with remains reportedly collected in polythene bags. Authorities have said DNA testing will be required for identification.

Most of the deceased are believed to be migrant labourers from Motihari.

District Collector Artika Shukla stated that a small quantity of explosive material appears to have triggered the blast. An FIR is being lodged by the Rajasthan State Industrial Development and Investment Corporation against the factory owners for illegal operations.

Further investigation is underway.

articles.title: Controversy in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar After “Purification” Ritual at Nageshwar Temple
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Controversy in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Maharashtra 🚨 In Rahimabad village of Sillod tehsil, a group of youths allegedly sprinkled gomutra inside the Nageshwar Mahadev Temple after former minister and Shiv Sena leader Abdul Sattar visited the shrine on Mahashivratri (February 15).

body.html:
Controversy in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Maharashtra 🚨

In Rahimabad village of Sillod tehsil, a group of youths allegedly sprinkled gomutra inside the Nageshwar Mahadev Temple after former minister and Shiv Sena leader Abdul Sattar visited the shrine on Mahashivratri (February 15).

Sattar had offered prayers at the temple during the festival. Later, the youths reportedly carried out what they called a “purification ritual,” claiming his presence had “contaminated” the sanctum. A video of the act has since gone viral.

Some of the youths allegedly objected to his entry, citing his non-vegetarian diet and religious identity, and said he should have taken darshan from outside.

The incident triggered sharp political reactions. Tushar Bhosale questioned Sattar’s entry into the sanctum, while Ambadas Danve termed the act “petty politics,” saying people of all faiths should be welcomed in temples. Chief Minister Eknath Shinde reportedly described the episode as “unfortunate.”

Sattar, a prominent leader from Sillod who previously served as agriculture minister and later aligned with the Shinde-led Shiv Sena faction, has not issued an immediate response.

No legal action has been announced so far. The episode has reignited debate over religious access and the politicisation of faith in the region.

articles.title: Missing Woman Case in Hassan Resolved; Police Say Disappearance Was Staged
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Missing case drama unfolds in Hassan, Karnataka 🚨 Priyanka (29), who went missing on February 12 after being last seen near the Belur bus stand, was traced safely after police revealed her disappearance was allegedly staged to leave her husband.

body.html:
Missing case drama unfolds in Hassan, Karnataka 🚨

Priyanka (29), who went missing on February 12 after being last seen near the Belur bus stand, was traced safely after police revealed her disappearance was allegedly staged to leave her husband.

Her clothes, slippers and vanity bag were found scattered near Kalkere Lake, triggering fears of murder over gold jewellery reportedly worth ₹20–30 lakh. Divers and drone teams were deployed, but no body was found.

Technical analysis of her mobile data led police to a lodge in Kunigal, where she was found with a man identified as David. Hassan SP Shubhanwita confirmed that Priyanka had allegedly switched off her phone, planted belongings near the lake to fake a murder scene, and travelled secretly to meet him.

Police said she did not want to continue her married life with her husband Rudresh and planned to start a new life with David, who was reportedly set to be transferred to Madhya Pradesh. She had also allegedly taken jewellery worth around ₹30 lakh.

After questioning, Priyanka was placed in a comfort centre for counselling and protection. No murder or abduction was reported, and the missing case has been officially resolved.

articles.title: Tension at Lal Darwaza After Attack on AIMIM Workers; Heavy Police Deployment
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Hyderabad (Telangana): Tension prevailed for some time at Lal Darwaza near the Maisamma Temple on the night of February 15, 2026, after a group of individuals allegedly assaulted workers of the All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM) and damaged the party flag.

body.html:
Hyderabad (Telangana): Tension prevailed for some time at Lal Darwaza near the Maisamma Temple on the night of February 15, 2026, after a group of individuals allegedly assaulted workers of the All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM) and damaged the party flag.

The Incident:
A group of AIMIM workers, including Arif Pathan Khan from Buldana district in Maharashtra, had travelled to Hyderabad to attend the party’s 68th Anniversary (Revival Day) celebrations at Darussalam.

According to reports, the workers were travelling in a car displaying the party flag when they reached Lal Darwaza near the Maisamma Temple. They were allegedly intercepted by a group of persons who abused them, physically assaulted them, and damaged the AIMIM party flag.

Eyewitness accounts claim that a police personnel was present nearby during the scuffle.

Complaint and Police Response:
Following the incident, AIMIM MLA Zulfeqar Ali reached the Moghalpura Police Station along with party workers and lodged a formal complaint.

Police registered a case and initiated an investigation. The Inspector and ACP of the Charminar division assured the party leadership that strict action would be taken against those responsible.

Security Measures and Current Situation:
To prevent further escalation, heavy security was deployed in Lal Darwaza and adjoining areas such as Gowlipura. The Hyderabad City Police, including the DCP Charminar Zone and Task Force teams, intensified patrolling and monitoring.

Authorities have stated that the situation is now peaceful and remains under close surveillance to maintain law and order.

Investigations are ongoing to identify and apprehend those involved in the assault.
